model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 5 (left) illustrates the proportion of SDPA output values falling below a threshold of 1e-2 across network layers, comparing pre-gating and post-gating conditions, alongside a derived sparsity metric based on average gating scores. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 20 in integer increments, representing sequential layers of the model. The vertical axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, indicating the proportion of values below the specified threshold. Three distinct lines are plotted: a dashed green line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03,” which remains near zero across all layers; a solid blue line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44,” which starts near 0.0 at layer 0, rises sharply to approximately 0.8 by layer 5, and then fluctuates slightly before plateauing near 0.8 through layer 20; and a dotted red line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33,” which begins near 0.0, increases more gradually than the blue line to reach approximately 0.6 by layer 10, and then remains relatively stable through layer 20. All three lines are marked with circular data point markers and show no visible error bars or shaded regions.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 5(left) displays the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a threshold of 1e-2 across network layers, comparing three conditions: the sparsity ratio before gating (represented by a dashed green line with circular markers), the sparsity ratio after gating (a solid blue line with circular markers), and the sparsity ratio after averaging the gating scores (a dash-dotted orange line with circular markers). The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 20 with linear spacing and integer tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with linear spacing and tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The dashed green line begins near 0.95 at layer 0, declines sharply to approximately 0.1 by layer 5, and remains near 0.1 through layer 20. The solid blue line starts near 0.44 at layer 0, drops to approximately 0.1 by layer 5, and stays near 0.1 through layer 20. The dash-dotted orange line begins near 0.33 at layer 0, decreases to approximately 0.1 by layer 5, and remains near 0.1 through layer 20. All three lines exhibit a steep decline in sparsity ratio from layer 0 to layer 5, followed by a stable, low sparsity ratio from layer 5 to layer 20.
model_annotations.English: Figure 5(left) illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a threshold of 1e-2 across different layers of a neural network, comparing three conditions: the sparsity ratio before gating (represented by a solid green line with circular markers), the sparsity ratio after gating (represented by a dashed orange line with square markers), and the sparsity ratio after applying an average gate (represented by a dotted blue line with triangular markers). The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 20 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The solid green line starts near 1.0 at layer 0 and declines sharply to approximately 0.2 by layer 5, then remains relatively flat. The dashed orange line begins near 0.44 at layer 0, drops to approximately 0.1 by layer 5, and continues to decrease gradually to about 0.05 by layer 20. The dotted blue line starts near 0.33 at layer 0, drops steeply to around 0.1 by layer 5, and then stabilizes near 0.05 through layer 20. The legend indicates that the average sparsity ratios for these three conditions are 0.03 (before gate), 0.44 (after gate), and 0.33 (after average gate), respectively.
